sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Catawba County?
sections.html:
The Catawba County Tax Office lists, appraises and assesses all real and personal property in the county, and it also collects the county's taxes. Its page gives (828) 465-8414 for general questions, and a separate line, (828) 465-8436, for tax relief appointments. Mail for relief applications goes to Assessor's Office, Attn: Tax Relief, Box 368, Newton, NC 28658-0368.

The county reports a fiscal year 2025 tax base of $31,422,508,337, a levy of $125,365,125 and a collection rate of 98.57 percent. The tax office has also earned the Certificate of Excellence in Assessment Administration from the International Association of Assessing Officers, which the county says makes it the fourth jurisdiction in North Carolina to hold it.

Apple Inc. is the largest taxpayer on the county's list at 4.70 percent of taxable assessed value, followed by Duke Energy Carolinas at 3.37 percent. The ten largest taxpayers together account for 12.15 percent. Your own bill depends on your parcel's value, the county rate and the fire district or town where the parcel sits.

sections.h2: What are the Catawba County property tax rates by district and town?
sections.html:
The county rate is .3985 per $100 of assessed value, and every parcel also pays either a fire district tax or a municipal tax. The county tax page prints the full list, and the table shows the main figures exactly as printed.

Others on the page include Cooksville at .0785, Propst at .072, Mtn View at .0855, Maiden Rural at .0983, Sherrills Ford/Terrell at .099, Conover Rural and Long View Rural at .10, Bandys at .1050, Catawba Rural at .117, Newton Rural at .121, St Stephens at .124 and Hickory Rural at .125.

A parcel inside a town or city pays that municipality's rate. A parcel outside pays the fire district rate that covers it. Read your bill or ask the tax office which one applies, then add it to the county rate for the combined figure.

sections.h2: When is the Catawba County revaluation, and how do appeals work?
sections.html:
Catawba County revalues every four years, current values took effect January 1, 2023, and the next countywide revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027. State law only requires a revaluation every eight years, so the county's four-year rhythm is shorter than the minimum. The county says staff are analyzing sales and market trends for the 2027 round.

The tax page states that the Board of Equalization and Review has adjourned for new appeals in the current tax year and that the next opportunity to appeal is January 2027. That lines up with the notices that follow a revaluation. The path starts with an informal review and moves up only if that fails:

  • When notices of value are mailed, ask the tax office how to request an informal review of your value, and use the form that comes with the notice.
  • If the informal review does not settle it, file with the county board of equalization and review. By statute you request a hearing in writing or in person before the board adjourns.
  • After the board decides, a notice of appeal to the state Property Tax Commission is due within 30 days after the board mailed its decision.

The county's revaluation page explains that revaluation updates values, not rates. Elected boards adopt the rate in the annual budget ordinance, which the county says is typically finalized in June. An appeal can reduce your value but cannot change the rate.

sections.h2: Which property tax relief programs does Catawba County offer?
sections.html:
The county tax relief page lists four programs: the elderly or disabled homestead exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment, and the AV-10 application for other exclusions. An owner may pick only one of the first three.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: you must be at least 65, or deemed totally and permanently disabled, on January 1, with household income under the limit and ownership of your home as of January 1. State law excludes the greater of $25,000 or half the appraised value. Applicants over 65 do not file a disability certification, and once approved you do not reapply every year, but you must report a move, sale, rental, deed change or income above the limit.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: up to $45,000 of assessed value of the permanent residence, with no income limit. The county asks for discharge proof plus VA certification of permanent and total service-connected disability, or proof of benefits for specially adapted housing.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: taxes are held to 4 or 5 percent of income, and the owner must have owned and occupied the home for five years or more. Deferred taxes are a lien, and a transfer of the property makes them due with interest for the current year and the previous three.

Applications for these three programs are due by June 1 each year, and the circuit breaker needs a fresh application annually. The AV-10 for religious, charitable, historic and similar exclusions is filed during January. NCDOR printed the income limit for 2026 as $38,800, with a 150 percent threshold of $58,200 for the circuit breaker.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax when you sell a house in Catawba County?
sections.html:
Taxes are settled at closing from the sale proceeds. The county's lien for a year's tax attaches as of the January 1 listing date, and the bill is due September 1. The county's own tax page says all property pays county tax plus a fire or municipal tax, so the payoff for a house in Hickory differs from one in a rural fire district.

Interest follows a fixed pattern: no interest on bills paid before January 6, then 2 percent through the end of January and three-fourths of one percent for each month afterward.

The circuit breaker is the item that surprises sellers. A transfer of the property is a disqualifying event, so the deferred amounts come due when the house sells. Ask the tax office for a statement that shows both the current bill and any deferred balance.

The deed side of closing runs through the Catawba County Register of Deeds. The seller pays the state excise tax of $1.00 per $500 of the price, or fraction, to the register before recording. Statewide recording fees start at $26 for an ordinary instrument up to 15 pages.

sections.h2: What does Catawba County look like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Catawba County sits in the western foothills of the Blue Ridge, covers 413 square miles, and was formed from Lincoln County in 1842. County offices use Newton addresses, and Hickory, Conover, Claremont, Maiden, Long View, Catawba and Brookford are the other municipalities on the county's tax page.

The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 170,172 residents, up 5.9 percent from the 2020 base, with 77,827 housing units. Of homes, 72.2 percent are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value for 2020-2024 is $241,600, and median gross rent is $965. The county issued 1,944 building permits in 2025, and median household income is $67,864.

Manufacturing and cable, gear and tape plants show up in the largest-taxpayer list, and the mean commute is 23.4 minutes. For comparison, the 2025-26 state rate table lists .3985 for Catawba County and .6270 for Caswell County.

faqs.q: What is the Catawba County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is .3985 per $100 of assessed value on the county's tax page. Every parcel also pays a fire district rate or a municipal rate, such as .46 in Hickory or .45 in Newton. Add the two for the combined rate on your parcel.

faqs.q: When do Catawba County property values change next?
faqs.a: The next countywide revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, after the one that took effect January 1, 2023. Catawba County revalues every four years. Appeals for the new values open once notices are mailed.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Catawba County tax relief?
faqs.a: Call (828) 465-8436 to book an appointment about tax relief, or (828) 465-8414 for general tax office questions. Relief applications can be mailed to Assessor's Office, Attn: Tax Relief, Box 368, Newton, NC 28658-0368. The deadline for the homestead programs is June 1.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay off deferred circuit breaker taxes when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. A transfer of the property ends the deferment, and the deferred taxes for the current year plus the previous three years come due with interest. Ask the tax office for the deferred balance before closing so the title company can pay it from the proceeds.

faqs.q: Is a disabled veteran exclusion available in Catawba County?
faqs.a: Yes. It excludes up to $45,000 of assessed value of a permanent residence and has no income limit. The veteran needs discharge proof plus VA certification of permanent and total service-connected disability, and the application is due by June 1.
